$summary: Viewport widths at which a page's layout changes. Three classes: narrow (below medium — the default, no token), medium, wide.

breakpoint.summary: The viewport widths where a page or template changes layout: narrow below breakpoint.medium, medium from it, wide from breakpoint.wide.
use: A page or template's region budget — when a rail becomes a drawer, when list-detail stops stacking.
JavaScript media queries (useMediaQuery) and the native build, which read the value directly.
CSS through the @custom-media names (--rata-medium, --rata-wide), expanded at build time — var() cannot appear inside @media.
dont: A component's internal layout. A component can sit in a sidebar as well as full width, so it responds to its own width with a container query, not to the viewport.
Hand-written rem or px in a media query — every layout breakpoint is one of these two.

scale.medium: 40rem (640px). Below it is narrow: one column, drawers instead of rails, bottom-nav on app surfaces.
scale.wide: 60rem (960px). The breakpoint the playground already used, now named. Panes sit beside the content from here.

notes: Two tokens for three classes: narrow is the default, so it has no threshold of its own. wide is medium × 1.5. Values are in rem so a reader who enlarges their root font size gets the narrower layout their text now needs.
